findings.title: Use of Untrusted Data in Signal Handling
findings.trigger: The child process sends a SIGINT to the parent process, which triggers the signal handler.
findings.assumptions: The signal handler is invoked based on user input or external events, which could be manipulated.

findings.title: OS Command Injection via Signal Handling
findings.trigger: The signal handler is invoked based on user input or external events, which could be manipulated to execute arbitrary commands.
findings.assumptions: The signal handler might execute commands based on certain conditions, which could be exploited.

findings.title: Race Condition in Fork and Signal Handling
findings.trigger: The race condition between the fork and the signal handling could lead to unexpected behavior.
findings.assumptions: The timing between the fork and the signal handling could be exploited to cause race conditions.

findings.title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
findings.trigger: The signal handler is invoked based on user input or external events, which could be manipulated to execute arbitrary commands.
findings.assumptions: The signal handler might execute commands based on certain conditions, which could be exploited.
